title: 17 Best apps for lawyers to boost productivity in 2026
summary: Find the best app for lawyers, from Quo for calls to Clio for case management and Fastcase for research. Free and paid options compared.
body_text: As a lawyer, client meetings and courtroom appointments may require you to switch gears quickly. Having an efficient set of apps that work on your computer and smartphone can make managing your law practice a lot easier. You’ll have access to the information you need when you need it, save time, and be able to offer a better client experience. In this article, we’ll give you an overview of the best apps for lawyers. We’ve categorized the apps so you can pick ones that best suit your law firm’s needs from relevant categories. If you’re a solo practitioner or part of a small firm, you don’t need to break the bank to build a solid tech stack. Many of the apps in this guide are free or available at a small-business-friendly cost. For example, with apps like Quo, Coffee, or HubSpot, you can stay organized and professional without much overhead. 17 Best apps for lawyers compared Here’s a side-by-side look at the tools in this research AI-powered legal assistant Contact sales Document analysis, drafting assistance, US case law research Communication apps When your client urgently needs help and your cell is unreachable, they’re likely to feel anxious. Instead, you can use communication apps to direct them to a colleague, let them know when you’ll be able to speak, or ask them to leave a message. Here are the best communication apps to help you save time and stay in touch with clients or colleagues. 1. Quo: Best business phone app for legal professionals Pros Unlimited calling and texting in the US and Canada Shared numbers for better collaboration No hardware required ⁠AI voice agent to take calls 24/7 Texting automations on every plan ⁠​Call recording AI features like call transcripts, call tags, and call summaries Role-based access and team controls to restrict access to sensitive client information Enterprise-grade communication and data encryption Cons No two-factor authentication*⁠ ⁠​*Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. For safety reasons, companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number. Clients expect to text and call a single, professional business number. Using a business phone system means you won’t need to give your personal number to clients, tribunals, courts, or opposing lawyers. Quo is a VoIP provider for law firms, designed for solo practitioners and small practices looking for a simple, modern way to manage phone communications. It can help you: Keep your team on the same page. Shared numbers let multiple team members manage calls and texts, so everything doesn’t fall on one person. It also gives everyone visibility into past conversations, even if they weren’t the ones who handled them. Here’s how Chris Sands, CEO of the family law office Hannon de Palma, uses shared numbers: “You might be in court and need to know what a paralegal said to the client three weeks ago. We can go into the paralegal’s number in their shared inbox and see: did the client actually agree to the thing that they’re saying they didn’t agree to, or did the other side say X and now they’re saying Y?” Respond professionally, even when you’re busy. Set auto-replies to let clients know you’ve received their messages and when they can expect a reply. Never miss an important call. Sona , an AI answering service for law firms , can answer basic FAQs, collect callback details, and take a messages. Track conversations over time. Automatically log call recordings, summaries , and transcripts so you can reference any past interaction — even months later. Connect with the tools you already use. Quo integrates with Clio and other tools in your workflow. This way, your client communications and case management stay in sync without manual data entry. Protect your client data. Quo supports data privacy standards like the California Consumer Privacy Act, or CCPA. It’s also SOC 2 compliant, helping you meet your ethical obligations around security and confidentiality. Read more about security at Quo . Samantha Kompa, Founder of Kompa Law , puts it plainly: “Quo is the most important tool in my tech stack to run my digital law firm.” Try Quo for free for seven days to see for yourself why growing law firms use this business phone platform. Key features of Quo Unlimited texting and calling in the US and Canada Available on web, desktop, and mobile so you can work from home or on the go as a virtual lawyer Texting templates for fast replies In-app task assignment On-demand and automatic call recording with searchable call history Call transcripts and summaries AI call handling with Sona Phone menu and smart routing Cold and warm transfers Voicemail transcription Business hours and after-hours call handling Call analytics and reporting Integrations with over 9,000 tools like Clio, HubSpot, and Slack Quo pricing Quo offers three flexible pricing plans for lawyers: Starter : $15 per user per month for texting and calling in the US and Canada, on-demand call recording, voicemail transcriptions, our AI voice agent, Sona, and more Business : $23 per user per month for automatic call recordings, AI call transcripts and summaries, CRM integrations with tools like Clio, custom ring groups, IVR, analytics and reporting, call transfers, and more Scale : $35 per user per month for AI call tags, priority chat and email support, inbound phone support, and dedicated onboarding Every Quo plan also comes with 1,000 free automation credits, or 10 Sona calls. If you need more, Quo offers five pricing tiers. That way, you can easily scale based on the number of calls you need to take. Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5 Sona tiers Free $25 per month $49 per month $99 per month $199 per month Included credits 1,000 credits/10 calls 4,000 credits/40 calls 10,000 credits/100 calls 25,000 credits/250 calls 60,000 credits/600 calls Overage rate per credit $0.01 $0.0075 $0.0065 $0.0055 $0.0045 Overage rate per call $1.00 $0.75 $0.65 $0.55 $0.45 *Calls under 15 seconds don’t count toward this amount 2. Coffee, formerly Legaler: Best secure video calling app Pros Offers a free tier Integrates with apps like Clio and Slack Video-meeting AI assistant Meeting analytics Cons Not as well-known as Zoom or Google Meet, so clients might need some initial guidance on usage Coffee, formerly Legaler, is a secure video meeting platform built for legal professionals. It offers encryption, admin controls, and a waiting room so only the right people can join your meetings. With Coffee, clients can also join meetings directly from their browsers, which means one less barrier to getting on a call. Already using Clio as your practice management system? You can integrate Coffee with it. This makes it easy to send meeting invites and automatically archive notes, agendas, and meeting details to the right matter. You can also connect Coffee to Slack to get notifications and set up meetings instantly for internal collaboration. Coffee also has an AI assistant, Piccolo. The AI communication tool handles transcription, meeting summaries, and live translation. It can also automate scheduling. The main caveat: it’s less widely recognized than Zoom or Google Meet, so some clients may need a quick heads-up before their first call. Coffee pricing Coffee is free to use. 3. Slack: Best for quick, internal communication Pros Offers a free tier Supports internal and external communication Integrates with tools like Quo AI assistant on paid plans Cons On the free tier, communication older than 90 days is deleted You can use Slack to keep your firm’s communication separate from client conversations. Create channels by matter or function, like intake, active cases, or operations. This way, questions, handoffs, and quick decisions don’t get lost in emails. Slack is especially useful for time-sensitive intake. The team can loop in the right attorney, confirm next steps, and keep a record of the decisions. You can also integrate Slack with Quo to get missed call notifications, texts, and voicemails right in your desired Slack channel. For example, if you forward texts to a Slack channel about a new intake or urgent client request, your team can coordinate a response more quickly. If you’re on a tight budget, you can use Slack’s free plan. Just know that it only saves up to 90 days of messages. Slack pricing Slack offers four pricing plans: Free: Up to 90 days of message history, integrations with 10 apps, 1:1 meetings, and 1:1 external messages Pro : $8.75 per user per month for basic AI with conversation summaries, unlimited message history, unlimited app integrations, group meetings, and group external messages Business+ : $18 per user per month for conversation summaries, workflow generation, AI search, daily recaps, and file summaries Enterprise+ : Custom pricing for enterprise-grade AI with enhanced search capabilities, multiple SAML configurations, EMM integration support, and native data loss prevention Legal practice management software Law firms have many moving parts. Law practice management software can help centralize operations and provide a single source of accurate information for research. You also need information at your fingertips to ensure the best outcomes for your clients. Here are some apps you can use for managing your practices and legal research: 4. Clio: Best practice management tool for integrations Pros Expansive integration library Offers AI and automation features to speed up legal work Users praise its robust billing and payment features Cons Integrations require an upgrade Users find the analytics tools to lack deep customization and granular insights Clio is a cloud-based law practice management solution. It offers several features to help you manage your practice remotely. For example, it helps you with client intake forms, billing, and document e-signing. Clio also has AI-powered tools for legal analysis, advanced document automation, court e-filing, and more. This way, you can spend less time on admin and more time on casework. You can also track time spent on specific tasks and set automatic reminders based on US court filing deadlines. Clio also has one of the more expansive integration libraries in legal tech. It connects with tools across communication, document management, and accounting. If you’re using Quo as your business phone, the Clio integration lets you keep client calls and messages synced with the right matter. That way, your communication history lives where your casework does. Clio pricing Clio’s pricing starts at $49 per user, and most plans have a free trial. But they don’t publicly list the legal app’s costs. You’ll have to get in touch with sales. 5. MyCase: Best for solo lawyers and smaller firms Pros Base plan is less limited than Clio Integrates with LawPay Users praise their customer support Cons Integrations require an upgrade Limited integrations compared to Clio MyCase is a case management and practice management platform for solo practitioners and small firms. It covers the core bases, like client intake, billing, document management, and time tracking. Compared to Clio, MyCase’s base plan is notably less restrictive. It gives smaller firms access to more features without having to upgrade right away. One standout feature is its native integration with LawPay, a legal-specific payment processor. This lets you accept credit card and eCheck payments directly from invoices. That way, your billing stays clean and there’s less friction with getting paid. The tradeoff is a thinner integration library overall. If your firm relies on a specific third-party tool, it’s worth checking compatibility before committing. Integrations beyond the basics also require a higher-tier plan. MyCase pricing MyCase offers three pricing plans: Basic: $50 per user per month for case and contact management, time entry, invoicing, trust accounting, online payments with next-day deposits, customizable reporting, and unlimited document storage Pro: $100 per user per month for automated workflows, unlimited eSignature and document generation, client intake forms, legal CRM, two-way texting, 70+ integrations, and AI writing and document assistant Advanced: $130 per user per month for an AI case assistant, advanced document automation, conflict check, split billing, desktop drive, and open API 6. CARET Legal, previously Zola Suite: Best for workflow automation Pros Built-in email management Offers automated workflows for scheduling and task delegation Cons Pricing isn’t available Charges an undisclosed implementation fee Limited integrations CARET Legal is a law practice management solution that serves small and mid-sized firms. Running a lean operation? You can track time, manage legal documents, handle billing and accounting, and use the CRM to manage prospects, all from a single platform. Where CARET Legal stands out is its workflow automation. You can build templates that automatically schedule tasks and calendar events based on matter type. Every time a similar case comes in, the right steps are already queued up. Let’s say you run a family law firm. You could set up a workflow that auto-schedules meetings and court appearances when you open a new dissolution of marriage case. It helps smaller teams stay consistent without relying on one person to remember every step. CARET Legal pricing CARET Legal offers three pricing plans. But they don’t publish their pricing upfront, and there’s an implementation fee on top of the subscription costs. Client intake and CRM apps Legal CRM and client intake tools are purpose-built for managing leads and onboarding new clients. They’re a good fit for smaller practices that don’t need a full practice management suite. 7. HubSpot CRM : Best free CRM Pros Offers a free functional CRM for small teams Integrates with more than 2,000 apps Modular pricing lets you pay only for the products you need Native integration with business phone systems like Quo Cons Pricing plans are mostly estimates; you still have to reach out to sales Too many features can make it confusing to navigate HubSpot offers a free CRM. It lets you centralize client information, conversation histories, and deal stages. For law firms, this can double as an intake pipeline. You can track new inquiries, consultations, and retained clients in one place so you don’t miss follow-ups. As your practice grows, you can add specific Hubs — such as Marketing or Sales — to access features like automatic lead scoring and forecasting. That said, most of HubSpot’s more powerful features require paid plans. Email sequences, automation, and advanced reporting are gated behind paid Hubs ranging from $9 per user to $3,600 per month. If you just need a CRM to manage intake and keep client communication organized, the free plan holds up well. You can also integrate it with Quo, which automatically logs your calls, texts, and voicemails directly into HubSpot . That way, every client interaction is on record without any manual entry. HubSpot CRM pricing HubSpot offers two plans for its foundational tools: Free CRM: $0 per month for its free cloud CRM for small businesses Starter: $9 per user per month for 500 HubSpot Credits, an AI-powered assistant, repeating tasks and task queues, and object tags For more advanced CRM features, Smart CRM plans begin at $45 per user per month and scale up from there. That said, the exact pricing depends on your use case. The HubSpot sales team told us it’s best to get in touch with them directly for an exact quote. 8. Lawmatics: Best for client intake automation Pros Marketing and intake automations Offers advanced features like round-robin scheduling, analytics and ROI tracking, and event management Built specifically for legal teams Cons Pricing not available User minimums on every plan can increase prices Client intake requires an upgrade Lawmatics is a legal-specific CRM and client intake platform. It covers lead management, automated intake workflows, ROI tracking, and analytics. It also helps you with lead tracking so you know where your leads are in the pipeline, where they came from, and what’s converting. What sets it apart from a basic CRM is its focus on pipeline movement and automation, not just contact storage. You can build intake workflows that trigger automatically when a new lead comes in. For example, you can send follow-up emails or route leads to the right attorney without team members intervening. There are also features like round-robin scheduling. This distributes incoming leads evenly across your team. For larger firms handling high volume of inquiries, Lawmatics adds a solid layer of operational structure. But Lawmatics isn’t really built for solo practitioners or very small teams. Every plan has user minimums, which can push the price up quickly. Plus, client intake automation — arguably the core selling point — requires an upgrade from the base plan. Lawmatics pricing Lawmatics doesn’t publish pricing publicly — you’ll need to schedule a demo to get a quote based on your firm’s size and needs. Legal billing and time tracking apps Consider these tools if you’re struggling to track billable hours accurately or want to send professional invoices and get paid faster. 9. Toggl Track: Best free time-tracking app for lawyers Pros Offers a free plan for up to five users Offers invoice creation, basic project management, and more than 100 integrations on the free plan Automated time tracking features, like the desktop activity tracker Cons Data compliance features require multiple upgrades QuickBooks integration requires an upgrade Not tailor-made for legal Toggl Track works well for lawyers who want accurate billable hour records without a complicated setup. It has a generous free plan that supports up to five users. It also includes invoice creation, basic project management, and access to 100+ integrations. On the tracking side, Toggl makes it easy to capture time across your entire workday. The browser extension lets you start a timer directly from the tools you’re already working in. You can also connect your calendar to automatically log time spent on phone calls, hearings, and consultations. Plus, it integrates with tools like Asana, Jira, and Clio, so you can track time without switching context. Use Toggl to assign hourly rates to projects, cases, or tasks to see what you’ve earned as you go. Then mark entries as billable or non-billable to cleanly separate client work from internal admin. One thing to flag: if you use QuickBooks for accounting, the integration requires a paid upgrade. Data compliance features are also gated behind higher-tier plans. This is worth keeping in mind if your firm handles sensitive matters with strict compliance requirements. Toggl Track pricing Toggl Track offers four pricing plans: Free: $0 for up to five users, with time tracking across web, desktop, and mobile, 100+ integrations via browser extension, Google and Outlook calendar integrations, and productivity reports Starter: $9 per user per month for billable rates, project time estimates and alerts, revenue and productivity analysis, QuickBooks integration, and team collaboration features Premium: $18 per user per month for profitability analysis, fixed fee projects, timesheet approvals, data accuracy features, fully customizable reports, and Jira and Salesforce integrations Enterprise: Custom pricing for personalized onboarding, a dedicated customer success manager, multiple workspaces, and volume discounts 10. Bill4Time: Best for robust tracking and billing features Pros Strong reporting features Offers expense management Clients praise its powerful invoicing Cons Limited integrations Some users find the interface outdated Bill4Time is a time tracking and billing platform for legal and professional services. It offers two main tracks, depending on what your firm needs: The Time & Billing plan . This is a solid choice for lawyers who want robust tracking and accounting without full practice management software. In addition to time tracking, it includes client portals, expense tracking, and document management. The Legal Pro plan . This includes time and billing features and adds legal-specific functions. It includes trust accounting and conflict checking. You also get contingency billing and LEDES export for e-billing compliance. One limitation to be aware of: Bill4Time’s integration library is thin. If you’re using tools it doesn’t natively connect with, you’ll need to rely on a third-party tool like Zapier to keep your data in sync across platforms. Bill4Time pricing Bill4Time offers four pricing plans: Time & Billing: $39 per user per month for time tracking, task and client management, client portal, expense management, accounting, invoicing, document management, QuickBooks integration, and calendar sync Time & Billing Enterprise: $69 per user per month for customizable data fields, a dedicated account manager, advanced data import, and advanced customizable reports Legal Pro: $59 per user per month for trust accounting, conflict checker, contingency billing, task workflows, LEDES export, and Box/NetDocuments integration Legal Enterprise: $89 per user per month for customizable data fields, custom LEDES export, a dedicated success specialist, and advanced data import Annotation and note-taking apps Need to take some quick notes during client calls or in the courtroom? These apps make note-taking easier. 11. Evernote: Best for search-first organization Pros Advanced search capabilities inside notes, PDFs, and images Evernote Web Clipper browser extension for saving online materials to client folders AI meeting note-taker Cons Not suitable for storing sensitive client data Not fully end-to-end encrypted While Evernote isn’t specifically designed as an app for lawyers, it has useful features that can make a lawyer’s job easier. For example, you can capture legal documents using your camera and edit them by cropping, rotating, or adjusting the folds. Then transfer them to the list of notes in your Evernote account. Evernote also lets you search within PDFs and images, making it easier to locate a specific clause or reference. Finally, you can use Evernote to save articles, case law, and legal blogs directly to client folders. From there, you can assign action items based on any note to stay on top of follow-ups. One important caveat: Evernote isn’t designed for storing sensitive client information. It doesn’t offer the security controls or compliance certifications — like SOC 2 or HIPAA support — that legal-grade tools do. So avoid saving anything covered by attorney-client privilege or confidentiality obligations. Use it for research, notes, and general organization, and keep sensitive case details in a more secure platform. Evernote pricing Evernote offers four pricing plans: Free: $0 for up to 50 notes, one notebook, 1GB monthly upload limit, 200MB max note size, image and document search, offline mode, PDF annotations, Tasks, and Web Clipper Starter: $8.25 per user per month for up to 1000 notes, 20 notebooks, up to three devices, 1,000 attachments, and IA features Advanced: $20.83 per user per month for unlimited notes, notebooks, attachments, and device syncs Enterprise Plan: Custom pricing for company ownership of all business data, a dedicated customer success manager, enhanced security and compliance, and 20GB monthly uploads and 2GB per user 12. OneNote: Best for Microsoft Office users Pros Advanced search capabilities inside notes, PDFs, and images Evernote Web Clipper browser extension for saving online materials to client folders AI meeting note-taker Cons Not suitable for storing sensitive client data Not fully end-to-end encrypted Microsoft OneNote is a solid choice if you’re already comfortable with Microsoft Office. Once you’ve taken notes, you can annotate or highlight them to review them more easily or add images or videos to your notes for context. Compared to Evernote, OneNote offers more ways to embed more information into your notes, such as spreadsheets. OneNote also has a Copilot AI feature that can summarize notes and help generate content more quickly. And if you’re taking notes in a hurry, you can use OneNote’s voice transcription feature. One organizational limitation to flag: OneNote uses a fixed Notebook > Section > Page hierarchy. This means each note lives in one specific location. Evernote is more flexible. It lets you apply multiple tags to a single note, so it can live in different locations. For example, a deposition memo could be tagged #ClientA, #Deposition, and #MotionToDismiss simultaneously. This might make retrievals faster, depending on your work. OneNote pricing OneNote is free to download, but premium features like collaboration tools require a Microsoft 365 subscription. Microsoft 365 offers three personal plans: Microsoft 365 Personal: $9.99 per month for one person, use on up to five devices, 1TB of cloud storage, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and OneNote desktop apps with Microsoft Copilot Microsoft 365 Family: $12.99 per month for up to six people, with each person able to use up to five devices and 1TB of cloud storage per person Microsoft 365 Premium: $19.99 per month for extensive Copilot usage and advanced AI image creation and editing in Microsoft Designer 13. iAnnotate: Best annotation app for iOS users Pros Allows for audio markups Built-in document scanning Supports iPad split screen for better simultaneous viewing of different documents Cons Only available on iOS devices Some users report crashes when marking up large or highly complex PDFs Folia’s iAnnotate lets you review and mark up documents directly on your device — PDFs, PowerPoint files, Word docs, images, and web pages. Markup options include highlights, notes, diagrams, and audio comments. This way, you can capture feedback in whatever format works best. You can also use it for note-taking and signing agreements. iAnnotate also lets you import files from your device or sync them from cloud storage services like Google Drive or Dropbox. One limitation: iAnnotate is only available on iOS and Mac, so it’s not an option if your team is on Windows or Android. iAnnotate pricing iAnnotate costs $9.99 on the Apple App Store for individuals. However, if you’re getting the app for your team, you might have to opt for iAnnotate Enterprise. Third-party sources note the pricing starts at a flat rate of around $5,000 per year and offers centralized management and deployment for organizations. For an exact quote, get in touch with their sales team. Cloud storage solutions Your team likely needs a simple way to pull up important documents at all times. You can use cloud storage to access documents from any computer or mobile device quickly. 🚩 Remember: It’s your responsibility to ensure your cloud storage solution aligns with professional standards These include, but aren’t limited to, standards outlined in the ABA’s Model Rules of Professional Conduct . For example, you must understand the benefits and risks of relevant legal technology . You also have to make “ reasonable efforts to ensure that the services [of an internet-based service to store client information] are provided in a manner that is compatible with [your] professional obligation.” 14. OneDrive: Best for Microsoft users Pros Included in Microsoft 365 subscription Personal Vault folder requiring additional authentication methods Cons Some users find file-sharing with external clients to be clunky Server-side encryption means Microsoft could theoretically access your data OneDrive is the best app for lawyers who already use Windows and Microsoft Office. It comes pre-installed in new Windows operating systems and seamlessly works in the background to sync files and folders to the cloud. You can install the OneDrive mobile app on your iPhone, iPad, or Android device. If your team uses both PC and Mac devices, Mac users can use OneDrive by installing the OneDrive app available in the Mac App Store. On the security side, OneDrive uses AES 256-bit encryption for files at rest and TLS encryption in transit. Microsoft 365 plans also have compliance features like HIPAA support, audit logs, and data loss prevention. For most standard client matters, that baseline is solid. That said, there’s one limitation to be aware of. Microsoft uses server-side encryption for most plans. This means they hold the encryption keys and could, in theory, access your data. Does your firm handle particularly sensitive matters, like criminal defense or national security? You may want to consider a zero-knowledge encryption solution where only you hold the keys. Make sure to review Microsoft’s documentation and speak with your IT provider before choosingOneDrive as your main storage. OneDrive pricing OneDrive is included with all Microsoft 365 plans. But the exact features you get, like storage amount, depend on the plan you choose. In addition to individual plans, Microsoft offers Business plans that may be more relevant for law firms. Prices shown are for the “With Teams” versions; plans without Teams are slightly cheaper. Microsoft 365 Business Basic: $6.00 per user per month for web and mobile versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, custom business email, Microsoft Teams, 1TB of cloud storage per user, and AI chat with Copilot Chat Microsoft 365 Business Standard: $12.50 per user per month for full desktop versions of all Microsoft 365 apps and webinar hosting with Teams Prefer not to pay for Teams? The same plans are available without it at $4.40 and $9.29 per user per month, respectively. 15. Box: Best for mid to large law firms Pros Top-tier security and compliance Granular user permissions AI integrations from the base plan Built-in e-signatures Cons Too costly for smaller firms Lacks matter-centric organization Business plans have minimum user limits Box is a cloud storage and content management platform built for mid- to large-sized law firms. It supports advanced document management needs, strict compliance requirements, and larger teams. With Box, you can collaborate on documents, assign tasks, and watermark sensitive files. You can also set granular user permissions. This way, you control who can view, edit, download, or share any given file. Need e-signatures? Box Sign handles e-signatures natively, starting from the base plan. Plus, Box AI lets you query documents, generate summaries, and extract key information directly from stored files. Security is where Box stands out. It offers AES 256-bit encryption, detailed audit logs, and data loss prevention. It also complies with frameworks like HIPAA, FINRA, and FedRAMP. The main limitations: Box isn’t built around matter-centric organization. You’ll need to create your own folder structure to match how a law firm works. And if you’re running a solo practice or small firm, the pricing can be a barrier. Box pricing Box offers five business plans, all with a minimum of three users: Business Starter: $5 per user per month for up to 10 users, 100GB of storage, 2GB file upload limit, unlimited e-signatures, and technical support during local business hours Business: $15 per user per month for unlimited storage, 5GB file upload limit, unlimited e-signatures, 1,500+ integrations, Box AI for single-file Q&A and content generation, and SOC 1/2/3 compliance support Business Plus: $25 per user per month for unlimited external collaborators and a 15GB file upload limit Enterprise: $35 per user per month for a 50GB file upload limit, advanced workflows, HIPAA and FedRAMP Moderate compliance support, native security classifications, and 1,000 Box AI units per month Enterprise Plus: $50 per user per month for a 150GB file upload limit, 2,000 Box AI units per month, threat detection, and 24-hour enhanced support Legal research software The right legal research tool can be the difference between billable hours well spent and time lost down a rabbit hole. Here are two options to consider: 16. Fastcase: Best mobile-friendly law library Pros Cost-effective Easy citation checking AI integration Cons May be too limited for large firms Fastcase is a comprehensive database for legal information and the US’s largest free mobile law library. It gives you access to a database of case law, statutes, constitutions, regulations, and court rules. It can cover most research needs for solo practitioners and small firms. If you need more, the full-featured desktop version unlocks additional features. Many bar associations include Fastcase access as a membership benefit, so it’s worth checking into before paying out of pocket. The platform also includes AI-powered search and citation checking tools. This can help you find relevant cases faster and verify that your sources are still good law. The main limitation is depth. Run a large firm that handles complex, multi-jurisdictional matters? Fastcase may not match the breadth of Westlaw or LexisNexis. But for most day-to-day research needs, it’s a strong and cost-effective option. Fastcase pricing Fastcase pricing generally starts at $65 per month for a basic plan. However, depending on your local bar association, you may already receive access for free. 17. Harvey AI: AI-powered legal assistant Pros Purpose-made for legal firms Natural-language UI Available on mobile Cons Pricing information not available Requires human review of outputs to ensure accuracy Targeted toward larger firms Harvey AI is a research and drafting assistant built specifically for legal professionals. It claims to be designed with enterprise-grade security and large language models trained on legal content. With Harvey, you can speed up research using sources like US case law and EDGAR filings or upload your own documents for analysis. It can compare contracts, summarize lengthy documents, and surface key information quickly. It can also assist with drafting, helping you move faster on work that’d otherwise call for long stretches of uninterrupted focus. While Harvey speeds up many parts of the legal research and review processes, you should always review the output for accuracy. Harvey isn’t intended to substitute legal judgment or advice. Harvey AI pricing Harvey AI pricing isn’t publicly available. You’ll need to contact them for a demo. Some third-party sources report it as ranging from $500 to $1,200 per user per month. Use Quo: The best VoIP system for lawyers You know you have to stay reachable. But you also need to stay organized when clients call, text, or leave voicemails. The right phone tool helps your firm respond faster and communicate professionally. It also records every interaction for compliance and future reference. Quo is built for exactly that. It gives small and growing firms a modern business phone system that works across devices. It keeps your team on the same page with shared numbers and conversation history and integrates with the tools you already use. That includes Clio and Slack. Missed calls are covered by Sona, Quo’s AI answering service. Client messages are automatically logged with call summaries and transcripts. And your personal number stays personal. title: Moreta Pay Is Live in Malaysia
summary: Pay local merchants by QR code across Asia and Latin America. Connect your bank or card, skip ATM fees, and pay like a local in your own currency with Moreta.
body_text: Malaysia just became a lot easier to travel through. Moreta Pay is officially live across the country, which means tourists, digital nomads and expats can now scan and pay at millions of Malaysian merchants using DuitNow QR, the national payment standard. Whether you're ordering roti canai at a mamak stall in Kuala Lumpur, buying char kway teow at a hawker centre in Penang or picking up sunscreen at a shop in Langkawi, you can pay in seconds with the same Moreta app you already use across Southeast Asia. No local bank account, no local phone number, no cash headaches. Why Malaysia, and Why Now? Malaysia has quietly become one of the most QR-friendly countries in Asia. DuitNow QR, the unified standard operated by PayNet under the oversight of Bank Negara Malaysia, connects the country's banks and e-wallets under a single interoperable QR code. One sticker at the till works for everyone. For Malaysians, scanning to pay is completely routine. Walk through any pasar malam and you'll see locals paying for satay and cendol without touching a single ringgit note. The problem, as always, has been foreigners. Local apps like Touch 'n Go eWallet, GrabPay and MAE either require a Malaysian bank account, a local SIM or a verification process that isn't practical for a two-week trip. Visitors end up carrying stacks of cash, hunting for ATMs and eating fees on every withdrawal. That's the exact gap Moreta was built to close, and Malaysia has been one of our most requested destinations. Now it's here. How It Works If you've used Moreta anywhere else, nothing changes. The same wallet that pays via PromptPay in Thailand or QRIS in Indonesia now speaks DuitNow QR too: Top up your Moreta wallet with your bank account or card in your home currency. Scan any DuitNow QR code at checkout. Look for the pink and white DuitNow logo — it's on counters, food stalls, taxis and market tables across the country. Review the details. You'll see the amount in Malaysian Ringgit, the exchange rate and the merchant name before anything moves. Swipe to pay. The merchant gets paid instantly in Ringgit, and you know exactly what it cost you. No fumbling with unfamiliar notes, no mental math at the counter and no surprise line items on your statement when you get home. DuitNow QR: One Code for the Whole Country DuitNow QR launched in 2019 as Malaysia's answer to a fragmented e-wallet landscape. Before it, every payment app had its own incompatible code and merchants displayed a small forest of QR stickers at the register. Now a single standardized code works across participating banks and wallets nationwide. For Moreta users, that interoperability is the whole point. It doesn't matter whether the stall owner banks with Maybank or CIMB, or whether they normally get paid through Touch 'n Go or Boost. If there's a DuitNow QR code on the counter, you can pay it. One scan connects you to essentially the entire Malaysian payment network. Where You Can Pay Almost everywhere, honestly. QR adoption in Malaysia runs deep, and you'll spot DuitNow codes in places that will surprise you: Mamak stalls and hawker centres serving nasi lemak, roti canai, laksa and teh tarik at all hours Kopitiams and cafés from KL's Chinatown to George Town's heritage streets Night markets (pasar malam) where vendors tape their QR code right to the table Convenience stores like 99 Speedmart, KK Super Mart and 7-Eleven Shopping malls including Pavilion, Suria KLCC and Mid Valley Taxis and ride-hailing , plus plenty of local transport options Hotels, guesthouses and homestays that accept digital payments From the food courts of Kuala Lumpur to the beach shacks of the islands, if there's a QR code, Moreta works. Save Money on Every Transaction The math on traditional travel payments in Malaysia is not kind. ATM withdrawals stack a local operator fee on top of your home bank's fee, plus whatever exchange markup gets baked in. Credit cards, where they're accepted at all, typically add 2 to 3 percent in foreign transaction fees — and plenty of the best food in Malaysia comes from stalls that have never seen a card terminal. With Moreta, you pay at transparent mid-market rates and see the full cost before you confirm. Over a two-week trip of daily meals, coffees, Grab rides and market runs, the savings are real. We broke down the wider fee problem in our guide on why traditional wallets fail travelers if you want the full picture. Built for the Way You Travel Malaysia rewards wandering. Most trips aren't just KL — you might land in the capital, take the train up to Penang for the food, ferry out to Langkawi for the beaches, then cross into Thailand or hop a cheap flight to Singapore or Indonesia. Moreta is built for exactly that kind of route. Because one wallet covers the whole region, you can pay with DuitNow QR in Malaysia on Monday, PromptPay in Thailand on Wednesday and QRIS in Bali by the weekend, all from the same app and the same balance. If you're planning a multi-country trip, our guide to how Southeast Asia's QR payment systems work is a good place to start. Getting Started Setting up before you fly takes a few minutes: Download the Moreta app from the App Store or Google Play . Create your account and verify your identity with your passport and a selfie. Connect a payment method and top up your wallet. Start scanning the moment you clear immigration. We'd recommend doing the setup at home over good wifi so you're ready to pay from your first teh tarik onward. One App, One Wallet, More of Asia Malaysia joins Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Cambodia, Laos and Mongolia on the list of countries where Moreta Pay is live, and it won't be the last. Our mission is simple: paying abroad should feel exactly like paying at home. No cash runs. No card fees. No juggling five local apps. Just scan, swipe and eat well.

Presenta una solicitud formal Dependiendo de las circunstancias, la entidad financiera puede requerir documentación adicional para analizar el caso. Comprende las limitaciones de los pagos inmediatos Es importante recordar que las transferencias inmediatas están diseñadas para completarse rápidamente, por lo que revertir una operación puede no ser sencillo. body_text: For job seekers, the search for a new role now comes with an added source of stress: determining whether an opportunity is real or an attempt to exploit their need for work. Employment scams rank among the most common types of consumer fraud, and they’re on the rise, according to the Better Business Bureau . Scammers use career boards, social media and generative AI to impersonate recruiters and promote fake openings that may appear legitimate. These scams frequently promise flexible hours and unusually high pay to lure victims into providing personal information, making upfront payments or granting access to financial accounts. SmartAsset analyzed the two most recent years of Federal Trade Commission data categorized as job scams to identify where reports increased the most. The study also measured how common these reports were in each state. Key Findings The frequency of reported job scams increased in every state. South Dakota saw the largest year-over-year increase, with reports rising by nearly 85%. Job scammers may target people facing a difficult labor market. Nevada had the highest annual unemployment rate in 2025. It also had the highest rate of reported job scams that year, at approximately 502 reports per 1 million residents. Low unemployment may have a modest correlation with fewer reported job scams. The six states with the fewest reported employment scams per 1 million residents all had unemployment rates well below the national average. Young adults report job scams more often than other types of fraud. While many scams target senior citizens, job scams are the most commonly reported fraud category among 18- to 34-year-olds. Expert Insight “Job seekers should always be cautious. Common warning signs are poorly written advertisements, recruiters who avoid video conversations, being asked to pay fees or share sensitive information, or offers that come fast and with high salaries. These types of scams have become more prevalent with hybrid and remote work.” — Gilbert Michaud, PhD Gilbert Michaud studies clean energy workforce development at Loyola University Chicago and is a Faculty Affiliate at the Gerald R. title: How to Speed Up Construction Document Review Without Losing Accuracy
summary: Estimators spend 38% of their time reviewing documents. This guide shows how GC teams cut that time by 80% without missing scope — and where AI fits in.
body_text: TL;DR Document review consumes 38% of estimator time — more than any other pre-bid activity. Most teams waste hours on the wrong documents, in the wrong order, without a repeatable system. A structured review sequence — drawings first, specs second, contract third — cuts wasted time without cutting accuracy. Purpose-built AI tools can reduce spec and contract review time by 80% and answer document questions in under 20 seconds. Speed without a process still produces missed scope. The goal is both. The Real Cost of Slow Document Review Document review is the single most time-consuming activity in pre-bid work. According to ASPE survey data, estimators spend roughly 38% of their working time reading specs, drawings, contracts, and addenda — before they price a single line item. On a 2,000-page project set, that time adds up fast. And the cost isn't just hours. It's what gets missed when the team is rushing. The Arcadis 2025 Global Construction Disputes Report puts the average U.S. construction dispute at $60.1 million. Errors and omissions in contract documents have been the top dispute cause for six of the last nine years. Those disputes start in pre-construction — during document review — when something gets skimmed or skipped. Speed matters. But not if it creates a $300K scope gap that your firm absorbs under "readily inferable" language. Why Most Document Review Is Inefficient Before fixing your process, it helps to understand where the time actually goes. Most teams waste time in three specific ways. 1. Reading in the Wrong Order Starting with Division 01 or the project manual is a common instinct. It feels thorough. But general conditions rarely contain the information that affects your number. Drawings and trade specs do. Reading front-to-back on a 2,000-page set means you spend hour one on boilerplate and hour ten on the stuff that actually matters. By then, you're tired and running out of time. 2. No Separation Between Roles When everyone reads everything, nothing gets read well. The estimator, the PM, and the pre-construction manager are all combing through the same spec sections with no clear ownership. Duplication doesn't create accuracy. It creates a false sense of security and a lot of wasted hours. 3. Addenda Management Gaps Addenda issued two days before bid day can change scope, modify specs, or override drawings issued six weeks earlier. Teams that don't have a clear addenda-tracking process often miss these changes entirely — or catch them after the number is locked. This is one of the anti-patterns documented in The Scope Gap Playbook : the five-minutes-before-bid review, where someone flags a late addendum after the bid is already built. A Faster, More Accurate Document Review Process Here is a structured sequence used by high-performing pre-construction teams. It's not complicated. The difference is discipline. Step 1: Skim the Full Set for Project Context (30 Minutes) Before reading anything closely, spend 30 minutes getting oriented. Review the drawing index, the spec table of contents, and the project manual cover sheet. You're not looking for details yet. You're answering three questions: What is this building? What's the delivery method? What's the scope boundary between the GC and the owner? This 30-minute pass prevents two hours of reading the wrong sections in depth. Step 2: Drawings First, Not Specs First This is Habit 1 from The Scope Gap Playbook's trade-specific scope chapter : drawings first, boilerplate second. Drawings show you what's actually being built. Specs tell you how. If you read the spec section for a roof assembly before you've looked at the roof plan and details, you're reading without context. Start with architectural, then structural, then MEP. Flag conflicts between drawing sets as you go. Those conflicts are where scope gaps live. A $45K stone-depth mismatch between civil/structural and architectural drawings on a single slab — documented in The Scope Gap Playbook — came from exactly this: nobody compared the two sets before bid day. Step 3: Read Trade Specs Against the Drawings Once you've reviewed the drawings, go through the relevant spec divisions. Read each section against the drawing you just reviewed — not in isolation. Watch for three things: Items shown on drawings that have no spec section Spec sections that reference products or assemblies not shown on any drawing Conflicts between spec language and drawing notes — especially on finish schedules and equipment schedules This cross-referencing step is where most scope gaps are found. It's also where most teams skip steps when time is short. Step 4: Contract Review — Scope Boundaries and Risk Flags After drawings and specs, read the contract with a specific focus: scope boundaries, allowances, alternates, unit prices, and risk-transfer language. Look for "readily inferable" clauses, "as per plans and specs" language in subcontract scopes, and any work that's described in the contract but not shown in the documents. "As per plans and specs" is the most-cited anti-pattern in pre-construction scope work. It transfers scope uncertainty to your subs — and when those subs get more sophisticated, they'll price the uncertainty back into you. As one Estimating Manager at a Canadian ICI GC put it: "We have less subs who just kind of a gentleman's agreement — they've become more quick to clarify that we're not including that one piece of scope." Step 5: Assign Document Ownership by Role Divide the review. Don't have everyone read everything. Lead estimator: drawings, trade specs for self-perform and key trade packages Pre-construction manager: contract, supplementary conditions, Division 01 Project manager (if involved pre-bid): project manual, addenda log, RFI register Each reviewer owns their section and logs findings in a shared tracker. One consolidated list is more useful than three partial reads of everything. Step 6: Log Addenda With a Timestamp Protocol Every addendum should be logged the day it's issued. Log the date received, the sections it affects, and whether it changes any line item in your estimate. Assign one person to own the addenda log. That person notifies the estimating team of any changes affecting scope or price — same day, not bid morning. Where AI Fits Into Faster Document Review A structured process gets you most of the way there. But even a well-organized team still spends significant time on tasks that don't require human judgment — searching for a specific spec clause, cross-referencing a product callout, or extracting every instance of a particular requirement across 80 spec sections. That's where purpose-built AI changes the math. Finding Answers in Large Document Sets Provision's Chat Agent lets estimators ask plain-language questions across the full project set — drawings, specs, contracts, RFIs, and addenda — and get cited answers in under 20 seconds. Instead of spending 20 minutes searching a 500-page project manual for the testing and inspection requirements on a structural steel package, you ask the question and get the answer with a document reference. Provision has processed over 66,000 construction documents and answered more than 50,000 queries across real project sets. The answers are grounded in the actual documents — not generated from a language model's training data. Scope Extraction at Scale For estimating teams managing multiple pursuits, the bottleneck isn't just reading documents — it's converting what you read into structured scope packages that subs can actually price. Provision's Scope Agent generates complete scope-of-work packages from construction documents in under 60 minutes. That replaces 30 to 40 hours of manual work per bid. It reads the drawings and specs together — not in isolation — and produces trade-specific scope packages with document references. That's the same cross-referencing logic described in Step 3 above, running automatically across the full project set. Risk and Contract Review Provision's Risk Review runs a structured checklist against your contract and spec documents, flagging risk items with 99.5% accuracy on pre-built checklists. For teams doing their own contract review, it cuts review time by 80% without cutting coverage. Provision has reviewed over $100 billion in project value and identified more than 1,000,000 risks across real construction documents. That's not a benchmark from a controlled test — it's production data from GC workflows. Why Generic AI Doesn't Work Here A common question from pre-construction teams in 2026: can we just use ChatGPT for this? The short answer is no — not reliably. Generic AI tools aren't trained on construction document structures. They don't understand the relationship between a drawing set and a spec section. They can't cross-reference a Division 23 equipment schedule against a mechanical drawing without hallucinating details that aren't there. Purpose-built tools for GC preconstruction are built around how construction documents actually work — project set ingestion, drawing and spec cross-referencing, RFI generation, and structured scope output. Generic AI produces prose. Construction estimating needs structured, cited, verifiable output. What Fast and Accurate Looks Like in Practice The EllisDon case study shows what this looks like at a real GC. EllisDon used Provision to review construction documents and identified risks that led to $1.8M in documented savings on a single project. That result didn't come from reading faster. It came from reading more completely — with a system that catches what manual review misses under time pressure. For teams managing five to ten active pursuits at any time, the compounding effect is significant. Cutting document review time by 80% per pursuit doesn't just free up hours. It creates capacity for more bids — or deeper review on the bids that matter most. The Five Things to Change This Week You don't need to overhaul your entire pre-construction process to get faster. Five changes make the biggest difference: Change your reading order. Drawings first, then trade specs, then contract. Stop reading Division 01 before you've seen the building. Assign document ownership. One reviewer per section. No duplication. One shared log. Build an addenda protocol. Log every addendum the day it drops. One person owns the log and notifies the team of scope changes the same day. Cross-reference before you price. Compare drawing sets against each other before reading specs. Conflicts between structural and architectural drawings are where the expensive gaps hide. Use AI for search, not judgment. Use a purpose-built tool to find spec clauses, answer document questions, and extract scope. Save human review time for the decisions that require it. Frequently Asked Questions How long should construction document review take? For a typical commercial project set of 500 to 1,500 pages, structured review by an experienced estimating team takes 20 to 35 hours. With purpose-built AI tools handling search, scope extraction, and risk flagging, that time drops to 5 to 10 hours for the same coverage — without reducing accuracy. What causes most errors in construction document review? The most common cause is reading documents in isolation rather than cross-referencing drawing sets against each other and against trade specs. Conflicts between structural and architectural drawings, or between a spec section and a drawing note, are the most frequent source of missed scope and pricing errors. Can AI replace manual construction document review? No — and it shouldn't try to. AI tools are most effective at the search, extraction, and flagging tasks that consume time without requiring judgment: finding spec clauses, cross-referencing product callouts, identifying risk language in contracts. Human review handles interpretation, trade context, and bid strategy. The best teams use both. What is the difference between Provision and ChatGPT for document review? body_text: Offering Comprised of Hospitality Assets in Connecticut and Florida DALLAS, July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — NexPoint , a multibillion-dollar alternative investment firm, today announced the launch of NexPoint Lodging II DST (the “Offering”), a Delaware statutory trust (“DST”) offering comprised of hotel properties located in Glastonbury, Connecticut and Bradenton, Florida. The Offering, NexPoint’s second dedicated hospitality DST vehicle, provides accredited investors with access to a two-property, nationally branded hospitality portfolio. NexPoint Lodging II DST includes the Homewood Suites® Hartford South – Glastonbury, an upscale extended-stay property, and the Courtyard by Marriott® Bradenton–Sarasota Riverfront, a premium select-service hotel on the Manatee River. Together, the properties offer complementary exposure to extended-stay and select-service hotel demand across two distinct markets: the Hartford, Connecticut MSA and the North Port–Bradenton–Sarasota, Florida MSA. The two properties are positioned to capture a broad mix of extended-stay, business, and leisure travel activity. The portfolio’s composition mitigates single-market concentration while providing exposure to a range of demand drivers across both regions. The Offering size is approximately $81.6 million. The portfolio’s recent and planned property improvements are intended to enhance asset quality, support competitive positioning, and drive operating performance. Homewood Suites® Hartford South – Glastonbury completed a comprehensive renovation in May 2024, including upgrades to guestrooms, common areas, and amenities which is expected to reduce near-term capital expenditure needs and support operating performance. Planned capital improvements at the Courtyard by Marriott® Bradenton–Sarasota Riverfront include guestroom and common-area renovations designed to enhance product quality, maintain competitive positioning, expand experiential offerings, and pursue incremental revenue opportunities. Both properties are managed by Dreamscape Hospitality, a Dallas-based hotel management firm with a national platform spanning more than 30 hotels across major brands. Dreamscape provides on-the-ground operational oversight, revenue management, and asset-level execution across the portfolio. NexPoint has sponsored DST/1031 exchange offerings for nearly 10 years, building a platform that has completed over $3.2 billion1 in acquisitions. The firm’s DST offerings span real estate subsectors, including multifamily, storage, life sciences, small bay industrial, semiconductor manufacturing, lodging, and marina. Lodging II DST is NexPoint’s 34th DST offering, adding to the firm’s deep experience and track record. About NexPoint NexPoint is a Dallas-based alternative investment firm with a multibillion-dollar platform spanning real estate , corporate credit and equities , and retirement solutions . The firm provides differentiated investment strategies for financial advisors, institutions, and individual investors through a range of vehicles, including mutual funds, public and private REITs, tax-advantaged structures, private funds, and separately managed accounts. For more information, including important risks and disclosures, visit nexpoint.com . This is not an offer to sell securities. An offer to sell interests in the DST may be made only to accredited investors pursuant to the Private Placement Memorandum of the DST, as may be amended or supplemented (the “Memorandum”). All investments involve risk. Investors must read the entire Memorandum prior to investing. Securities offered through NexPoint Securities, Inc., a member of FINRA/SIPC. NexPoint Securities, Inc. is an entity under common control with the sponsor of the Offering.
